title: World Cup 2026 LIVE: FIFA under more fire for Balogun saga, Kane defends Tuchel's comments, Messi ready to play England for first time | talkSPORT
text:
England beat Norway 2-1 to advance into their just their fourth semi-final at the tournament.

Jude Bellingham was once again the Three Lions' hero as he scored twice, with England now facing Argentina for a place in the final.

Lionel Messi and co. needed extra time to beat Switzerland in what was another dramatic match for the World Cup holders.

You can follow all of our World Cup tips & predictions over in our betting hub, along with the best betting offers.

Follow our live blog below all summer long for regular updates...

Former Liverpool defender Ibrahima Konate has sent a warning to his French teammates ahead of facing Spain.

La Roja meet Les Bleus in a mouthwatering semi-final on Tuesday.

The winners will take on England or Argentina in the final on Sunday.

Now, one player who is probably yet to show his best is Lamine Yamal.

He has one goal in the tournament after returning from injury.

But Konate feels Spain are much more than just Yamal.

He said: "We don't really think about it because the Spanish team is an exceptional nation with a lot of quality.

"The goal is not to focus on one player because the entire team can hurt.

"It just about Lamine, it is all of them."

We just had news about Argentina requesting to wear their away kit, and now it looks like FIFA have confirmed that Spain will be wearing their away strip as well.

In the pre-match pack, it shows that France are in all blue, but La Roja have had to ditch the red.

Instead, they'll be in their all-white kit.

It's interesting that has happened because there would be no clash at all.

Argentina have reportedly asked to FIFA if they can play in their away kit for the World Cup semi-final with England.

Argentina are the designated away team for Wednesday's match in Atlanta.

However, they would be able to wear their iconic blue and white home jersey as there's not a clash with England's white kit.

Reports in Argentina suggest Argentina have submitted a request to FIFA that they wear their all-blue kit.

They have worn it just once so far in the tournament.

Former England player Andros Townsend defended Jude Bellingham after going up against manager Thomas Tuchel.

Tuchel was not entirely happy with England's performance against Norway as they booked their place in the World Cup semi-final.

In response, Bellingham said 'whatever' and dismissed his manager's comments.

Speaking on talkSPORT, Townsend said: “I think Bellingham was set up a little bit by the reporter because the reporter made it seem like Thomas Tuchel was having a go at the performance.

“He wasn't having a go at the performance. He was merely saying that the mentality was what won them in this game. They weren't at their free-flowing best but their mentality and their braveness to get on the ball saw them over the line.

“Whereas when Jude Bellingham had his interview emotions were running high. He just helped his team get into a semi-final. It was almost framed as if that the manager was unhappy with the performance and so it brought out a spiky response.

“But come on guys, we're in the semi-final of a World Cup. Let's get behind our team, let's get behind our manager. Let's stop trying to create headlines that our star players are going up against our manager.

“It's not good for us, it's not good for us going into that game against a nation who everyone is on side. Everyone is together. Their support is the best.

“The South Americans are the best I've seen in the world. I've done Argentina and I've gone to Colombia. They're the most passionate. I’ve seen commentators crying when they scored the winning goal against Switzerland.

“So let's try and have a bit of that togetherness going into Wednesday because we're going to need it.”

The officials for France and Spain's World Cup semi-final has been announced.

El Salvador's Ivan Barton has been given the job of officiating the key clash on Tuesday - with commentary live on talkSPORT.

Barton made a name for himself earlier in the tournament when he sent off Paraguay's Miguel Almiron for covering his mouth.

The World Cup semi-final will be his fourth match of the tournament.

David Beckham was welcomed into the England dressing room in Miami to be part of a special moment.

The Three Lions icon was handed his legacy cap by Harry Kane, joining all of the nation's stars with the gift.

Every player who has represented the country now gets a cap to signify their role in England's footballing history.

Harry Kane gave the gift to Beckham, saying: "Sir David, thank you for coming. Thank you for having us. First and foremost, as you know, we have the Legacy Caps now. Number 1078 for you.

"I speak on behalf of me, and I think a lot of the guys in the room and a lot of ex-players as well. You were a big role model for me, a big inspiration.

"I think every time you wore the England shirt, you showed desire, you showed passion, you showed what it's like to lead your country.

"Five major tournaments, you played at three World Cups. Obviously, you're one of England's all-time greats, so it's an honour for me to present this to you."

After the room clapped for the legend, Beckham replied: "Thank you, and firstly, welcome to Miami. Obviously, this is very special, so thank you to you and to everyone here.

"I know you've probably heard it all before, but you're making everyone proud with everything that you're doing, not just on the field but off the field, and that's really important to the fans and to everyone back home.

"I know you feel it because you all hear everything about what is going on at home, and you're making everyone proud, so continue it.

"It's been incredible. You've got a leader here [Harry Kane] who leads by example, on and off the field, but every one of you is a leader, and that's been apparent in this World Cup.

"So continue to do it, continue to make us all proud. Thank you again."

Uruguay legend Diego Forlan is set to become his nation's new manager, replacing Marcelo Bielsa in the hot seat.

But there's a catch: he may only be in charge for eight months.

The Uruguayan Football Association confirmed on Sunday that Forlan had been appointed interim head coach.

His contract will only run until March 2027.

At that point, the Uruguayan FA will assess his performance and either extend his stay or appoint a new boss.

On top of his new role with the senior set-up, Forlan will keep serving as Uruguay's U20s head coach at the same time.

The ex-Manchester United striker is his country's third all-time top goalscorer and he also still has the seventh-most caps.

He takes over from Bielsa, who stepped down following a World Cup campaign that saw the nation fail to win a game.

The decision to suspend a ban for Folarin Balogun was taken solely by the chairman of FIFA’s disciplinary committee, Mohammad Al-Kamali.

This is extremely unusual. Although FIFA do hear cases with a sole arbiter often, it’s traditionally one of the other 17 members and deputy chairman Jorge Palacio.

Precedent-setting cases usually have a three-person panel.

So, the decision for Al-Kamali to hear the case alone will raise further questions for FIFA.

FIFA claim the decision was made independently but have faced backlash after talkSPORT exclusively revealed Donald Trump asked FIFA President Gianni Infantino to review Balogun’s sending off against Bosnia.

Trump subsequently confirmed his intervention, and Balogun was handed a suspended one-match ban. He played in USA’s 4-1 loss to Belgium.

The decision has raised questions given all other red cards at the tournament have been immediately served, including Jarrell Quansah, who is serving a two-game ban for his red against Mexico.

The FA had no ability to appeal despite the fact that US Soccer's case centred on excessive use of slow-mo and still images to misrepresent the incident, yet VAR showed similar images prior to Quansah’s sending off.

England captain Harry Kane has defended manager Thomas Tuchel for his negative review of the win over Norway.

Tuchel took a critical approach to his post-match interview in Miami, with Jude Bellingham and Djed Spence disagreeing.

However, Kane has leapt to his defence, admitting that the Three Lions were not at their best during the 2-1 victory.

The skipper said: "When he sees us train and sees the closeness of us and sees what we can do, especially with the players we have, the way we attack, our one-on-ones and the skills, he just wants to see that version of us.

"He knows as much as anyone that it's not as simple as that, we're playing against good opposition and good teams. He's trying to drag it out of us and we know ourselves we have another level we can reach.

"We haven't seen that yet, we've shown it in glimpses. Against Norway, it was in glimpses. But we haven't had full control that we would like and I feel we can have.

"We'll be playing against one of the best teams in the world in the semi-final, so the most pleasing thing is we are in a semi-final and still feel we can improve.

"But I don't think it is something to get really over the top about. We are showing a lot of good things."

The World Cup semi-finals take place this week between the top four seeded nations in the tournament.

Hype will already be building and fans are finding out which kits the teams will be wearing during the last four.

France vs Spain

It is currently expected that France will be donning their home strip, that included a navy blue shirt with a white collar.

The kit also included white shorts and red socks.

They're facing Spain, who are set to play in their alternate white shirts, red shorts and white socks on Tuesday night.

England vs Argentina

As for England's World Cup semi-final, they are expected to be playing in their all-white home strip for the game.

Meanwhile, Lionel Messi and co. will be in their black and navy shirts, with a swirl design for Wednesday's clash.

The Argentina kit also includes black shorts and socks.

Incredibly despite Lionel Messi doing everything on a football pitch, he has never played against England.

Well, all that changes on Wednesday in the World Cup semi-final.

The Argentine superstar is looking to take his country to the final, and he is looking forward to the challenge of facing England.

He said: “Facing England will be special! It’s my first time playing against England. I’ve played against just about everyone except them.

“They are a great team, a football powerhouse, it’s always exciting to face opponents like that”.

FIFA and FIFPRO, the global players' union, are set to hold talks over playing games in extreme heat.

This follows concerns over some of the conditions that players have been exposed to in the World Cup and Club World Cup last year.

England's game against Norway was 33 degrees, with a feel like temperature of 45 degrees.

More concerning was the wet bulb temperature, which was at 31 degrees.

The recommended cut-off point for that is 28 degrees because it impacts sweating.

Under FIFPRO regulations, the match wouldn't have kicked off when it did.

However, there are no agreed regulations, so the game went ahead.

That is how Alf Inge Haaland described Norway following their 2-1 defeat to England in the World Cup quarter-finals.

Two decisions went against the Norwegians that proved to be crucial.

The first error was that the ball hit the overhead camera wire before Jude Bellingham's first goal.

That should have resulted in play restarting with a Norway goal kick.

They then had a goal ruled out for a foul by Erling Haaland on Elliot Anderson.

And after the game, Haaland senior said: "Well done Bellingham and referee.

"Really? Saved by the referee. Hope you win the WC now. But feel we got robbed today."

Alan Pardew believes that starting Declan Rice for England against Norway was an error by Thomas Tuchel.

The Arsenal midfielder only managed 45 minutes of the 2-1 win.

He was replaced at half time by Eberechi Eze.

In the build-up to the match, Rice had been dealing with illness, while he's had neural pain throughout.

Speaking on talkSPORT, he said: "Something I learned as a manager when I had a player ill, a good one of my regular players, when I was a young manager I always played them Thinking that they're that good.

“But what I'm saying is when you're playing top level for sport, if you're sick or poorly and they never played well, never.

“So of course when I got older and I realised that if a player wasn't right I wouldn't play him. They just can't produce, they haven't got the emotional thought process to be happy and be good.

“They're kind of down and that and their game goes down. Dec looked like he looked down yesterday, didn't he? You only had to look at him. So, he wasn't like buzzing and being the Declan rice that we know.

"So that was a mistake that Thomas made there.”

Sean Dyche believes England were lucky to not be 2-1 down to Norway last night.

The Norwegians made it 2-1 only to see the goal chalked off by VAR for a foul on Elliot Anderson by Erling Haaland.

But Dyche believes that the foul had little impact on the goal being scored.

Watch his thoughts below.

He said: "I thought we got a little bit lucky with that one.

"It's nothing that big to do with the goal. I don't think it is that big of a deal.

"I don't think Anderson can have a true impact.

"So, I get why they are disgruntled."

Following Jude Bellingham disagreeing with Thomas Tuchel after England's 2-1 win over Norway, Noni Madueke also didn't agree with the manager.

Speaking in the immediate aftermath of the victory, Tuchel criticised England's performance.

Bellingham hit back and so has Madueke.

When asked about the comments, the Arsenal winger said: "That's his opinion.

"I have a different opinion maybe.

"But it is what it is. That's his opinion."

We all love Jason Cundy at talkSPORT, but the nation has fallen in love with him in 2026 even more so than they already did.

And he's even now got the outgoing Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer to use one of his bits.

Following the win over Norway, Starmer tagged the Norwegian Prime Minister in a tweet and mentioned that they'd took 'one hell of a beating'

We all know this is part of 'Has Anyone Seen'.

But to see the PM do it is truly something else.

Knighthood for Jase in the PM's leaving honours?

You often can tell just how good a footballer is when other top professionals go onto social media and make a point of praising them.

And that happened twice last night as Jude Bellingham dragged England to a World Cup semi-final.

Jurrien Timber and Toni Kroos both tweeted their praise for the England star.

He now has six goals at the World Cup.

There were suggestions that England's equaliser against Norway should have been ruled out due to the ball hitting an overhead camera cable.

Now, FIFA denied this was the case.

But 3D camera footage contradicts the line FIFA have been running with.

Take a look below and make up your own mind.

A huge thanks to Jude Bellingham's mother.

The England star was walking a tightrope for a yellow card that would have seen him banned for the semi-final.

But he managed to avoid it, and we need to be thanking his mam.

Speaking after the match, Bellingham said: “My mum's been telling me all week to watch my language, watch my tackles, watch my face, watch my emotions.

“I think she drilled it into me all week about being careful of that yellow card."

On behalf of a nation, thank you.

England and Argentina haven't plated each other that much, but it is the Three Lions who have the better recent record.

England are unbeaten in their last three meetings with the South American giants.

England beat Argentina in the 2002 World Cup to avenge 1998 when David Beckham was sent off.

And at that point, England hadn't beaten Argentina since 1980.

So, it's a mixed bag.

England vs Argentina: Results

Another game, another two goals for Jude Bellingham, who is doing everything he can to take England to World Cup glory.

But Max Scott wants some accountability.

He wants Craig Hope to apologise for suggesting that Bellingham shouldn't go to the World Cup.

The Real Madrid star is on six goals for the tournament now and is in Golden Boot contention.

Speaking on Weekend Sports Breakfast, he said: "When is Craig Hope going to apologise and hold his hands up for the absolute stinker he had.

"Just over a year ago, he wrote an article that Bellingham should be left out of the World Cup squad because, 'he's a divisive soloist'.

"For me, that article was indicative of this overreaction and vilification of one of the greatest talents this country has ever produced.

"He's a matchwinner, and he's the first person since Diego Maradona to score two in back-to-back knockout games.

"When you get something so wrong, you have to apologise."

Jude Bellingham got another 10/10 in Adrian Durham's player ratings.

Bellingham scored twice in England's 2-1 extra-time win over Norway to book their place in the World Cup semi-finals.

"He must be shattered after carrying most of his teammates," Durham said.

Read how the rest of the Three Lions players did in the ratings below.

Lionel Messi will play against England for the first time in his career in the World Cup semi-final.

Argentina booked their place in the final four with an extra-time win over Switzerland.

Speaking after the match, Messi said: "Yes, absolutely, matches against the big national teams are always special, and I’ve never played against England before, so it will be a unique game.

“It’s a World Cup semi-final, and now we’ll rest and prepare for it. We’ve put in a huge effort after going through two extra times and then another match, and that shows sometimes.”

Argentina are looking to retain the World Cup after lifting the trophy in Qatar four years ago.

Senegal have confirmed that they have sacked manager Pape Thiaw after the country suffered World Cup knockout heartache last week.

The Teranga Lions were 2-0 up late on against Belgium in their last-32 clash before a shocking collapse ultimately ended in a 3-2 defeat.

A statement said: "The Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) informs the public that following the meeting of the Executive Committee held this Saturday, July 11, 2026, it was decided to initiate a procedure to terminate the functions of the national coach, Mr Pape Thiaw, as well as his entire technical staff.

This decision comes after the elimination of the Senegal national team in the round of 32 of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

"After a thorough evaluation of the sporting results and prospects of the national team, the Executive Committee deemed it necessary to initiate this procedure in the best interests of Senegalese football.

"To this end, the President of the Senegalese Football Federation, Mr Abdoulaye Fall, has been mandated to bring this decision to the attention of the competent authority and to ensure official notification to the person concerned, in accordance with the statutory, regulatory and contractual provisions in force.

"Also, the Executive Committee mandated the President to take all necessary measures for a genuine reorganisation of all national teams.

"Furthermore, the President of the Senegalese Football Federation will hold a press conference on Monday, July 13, 2026, at 4 p.m., at the Léopold Sédar Senghor stadium.

"This meeting with the media will be an opportunity to present the reasons for this decision, to take stock of the situation of the national team and to discuss the prospects for the future.

"The Senegalese Football Federation reaffirms its commitment to act in accordance with procedures, transparency and good governance, with the sole objective of preserving the best interests of Senegalese football."
